notes.decision: Translated 'quenched' rather than 'afflicted'. ϩⲱϣⲙ has a primary range of 'oppress, afflict' (cf. accumulated ϩⲉϣϩⲙϣ), but in collocation with fire/burning and the Enemy as object, the related sense 'extinguish, quench' fits the cosmic context better — the Living Fire's garment overpowers and quenches the Enemy's expanse.

Translated 'expanse of the Enemy.' ⲟⲩⲟⲥⲉ from ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲉ 'spread out, become wide' yields a substantival 'expanse, breadth.' The Enemy's expanse (his outspread cosmic territory) is what the fire-garment brings down.

Translated 'the four kinds.' ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ = 'the four' (in vocabulary) + ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'kind, category' (in vocabulary) yields the cosmological 'four kinds' — i.e., the four other garments (wind, water, light, air) listed above. The collective enumeration matches the Manichaean schema of five elements/garments.
Translated 'be able to encircle him.' ϣ- modal prefix 'be able' + ⲭⲱⲧⲉ (Lyc. = ⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'surround, encircle' — already in vocabulary). The Enemy's burning could not encompass the Living Fire.
Marked break_after=true. The 'leer' signals end of the previous kephalaion before chapter 52 begins. Chapter heading occupies lines 24-25 in the standard double-numeral wrap format.

Translated 'the foremost Darkness which reigned over him.' ⲛⲧⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ = ⲛ̄-ⲧ-ϣⲟⲣⲡ 'of the foremost' (Lyc. ⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧ in vocab); ⲛⲧⲁϩⲟⲣⲟ = relative perfect 'which reigned' (cf. accumulated ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'reign over').
